author: Dr. Lurie Skincare
deck: A practical morning-and-evening routine built around consistency, comfort, and sun protection.
description: A concise, first-person guide to a simple skincare routine with gentle cleansing, moisturizing, sunscreen, and cautious use of optional treatments.

public.body: If I were building a skincare routine for myself, I would make it deliberately boring. Skin usually does not need a crowded shelf or a new experiment every week. I would choose a few comfortable products, use them consistently, and change only one thing at a time.

images.alt: A simple morning skincare routine with cleanser, moisturizer, and sunscreen
A calm evening skincare routine with cleanser and moisturizer

public.title: Simple on purpose

public.body: I would start with a gentle cleanse, or simply rinse if my skin felt dry or comfortable from the night before. Next would come a plain moisturizer when needed. The final step would be broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher on exposed skin. I would treat sunscreen as the non-negotiable part, not the decorative finale.
public.title: Morning

public.body: At night, I would remove sunscreen, makeup, and the day with a gentle cleanser. Then I would moisturize while the routine was still easy to remember. If I wanted to address a specific concern, I would add only one targeted product, introduce it slowly, and watch for persistent stinging, redness, or peeling instead of assuming discomfort means it is working.
public.title: Evening

public.body: I would skip harsh scrubs, frequent product switching, and the urge to copy every trending routine. A short routine is easier to evaluate: when something helps or irritates, the cause is clearer. I would also give ordinary habits time to work before buying another solution.
public.title: What I would skip

public.body: This is a general routine, not individualized medical advice. Ongoing acne, rashes, pain, or significant irritation deserve guidance from a qualified clinician.
public.title: A final note
